newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan tycoon starts US$400 mln Asia-Pacific fund.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan tycoon starts US$400 mln Asia-Pacific fund.

text.p: Taiwan tycoon Jeffrey Koo has raised US$400 million in international capital and formed a private Asia-Pacific investment fund, Crimson Asia Capital Holdings Ltd, Koo aides said on Monday.

The fund went into operation on July 1 with Koo as its chairman and Koo's son, Jeffrey Koo Jr, in day-to-day charge as executive director, aides said as the Koos and others gathered in Taipei for a formal announcement of the fund.
The senior Koo is chairman of Chinatrust Commercial Bank, one of Taiwan's most ambitious private banks, and has been exploring ways to pioneer investment banking in Taiwan.
Koo aides said Chinatrust had no stake in the new fund.
Koo, addressing the news conference, described the new fund as an investment bank in its own right with no connection to Chinatrust.

"This fund aims to expand Taiwan's service in the investment banking sector because that is an area where Taiwan lags behind foreign banks," Koo said. "This is a necessary step in the internationalisation of Taiwan's banks."
Initial investment into the fund already has been secured from four regions -- the Middle East, Europe, the United States and Asia -- each with roughly one-fourth stakes, Koo said.
The powerful Koo family itself holds 10 percent, he said.
Koo declined to identify other investors.
The fund was expected to generate an investment return of 30 percent, Koo said. The initial capital would be fully invested within five years, after which more funds would be raised.
Koo gave some details of how the funds would be invested, saying 25-30 percent would be poured into Taiwan itself.
The rest would divided among various Asian countries, mainly the Philippines, Japan, Hong Kong, mainland China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand.
Ten percent would be earmarked for investment in listed shares, while the rest would be invested in promising unlisted firms, Koo said.
Ten percent of the capital will be steered toward real estate investments, he added.
The fund is registered in the Cayman Islands, Koo said.
